comments.body:
The time tables on the D-CHAB website were always accurate in my case. Presence is required in all practical laboratory courses, but not in lectures or exercises. Nonetheless, I would say that working on Fridays could become a problem already in the second semester, as this year, all first-year pharmacy students had the „Grundlagen der Biologie I“ practical course either on Friday morning or afternoon. In the third semester the Organic chemistry lab might take place on Fridays, although the professor there is very understanding and if you have a good reason you can ask to be put in the group, which has their courses on Tuesdays & Wednesdays. In the third year presence is required every afternoon and even being sick for more than a couple of days might lead to not passing the course in some practicals, especially in the shorter ones. Generally, I would say that working on the side in the third year is very demanding but there are always exceptional people who manage. In my experience only around 20% of people manage to complete the bachelor course in 6 semesters and many want to or have to add one or two semesters. This is absolutely common and would probably allow you to be able to work a bit more outside of school.

In any case, you can really look forward to your studies here. It will be challenging, but especially the third year is very interesting and there are a lot of fun people around :)
I you have any questions don‘t hesitate to dm me.
comments.author: DreamingLab
